beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:setting the scene, measured][tune:level]A handwritten book of two hundred and ^forty pages. [act:building the picture][tune:level]Written in an alphabet ^nobody knows. [act:the strangest one, with wonder][tune:fall]Painted with plants that ^don't exist.

[d:tension][act:admiring, steady]It's called the Voynich ^manuscript, and for over a century it has beaten ^every codebreaker. [act:hushed, the real puzzle][tune:rise]So the real question: is anything written there at ^all?

[d:calm][act:plain facts, reassuring]Its pages are ^calfskin, and a calf was once ^alive. [p:0.93][act:explaining, patient]Living things hold a trace of radioactive carbon, which fades after death at a steady pace, like a candle burning ^down: measure what's left, and you know when the animal ^died. [act:the result, plain]Four samples say {1404|fourteen oh four} to {1438|fourteen thirty-eight}. [act:plain, reassuring]Truly ^medieval.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:storytelling, a little wonder]By about {1600|sixteen hundred}, the book was in ^Prague, at the court of an emperor who collected ^wonders. [act:plain, tracing it]Later, it was sent ^south, to a famous ^scholar.

[d:build][act:making the case, brisk]Now, the case for a real ^language. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]In every language, the most common word turns up about twice as often as the ^second, three times as often as the ^third, and so on down a smooth ^staircase. [act:the point, building]Count the words in this book, and you get the ^same staircase. [act:one more point, building]Some words crowd into one ^section of the book, and match its ^pictures. [act:a surprising detail, lightly]And studies of the handwriting find ^five different scribes.

[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:the counterpoint, crisp]But here's the case ^against. [p:0.93][act:explaining, playful]Play a game of guess the next ^letter. [act:explaining, clear]In English, after a q, bet on a ^u; most letters keep you ^guessing. [act:the point, crisp]In this book, the next letter is far ^easier to guess than in any known ^language. [act:puzzled, slower]And words repeat in strange ^runs, the same word two or three times in a ^row@line.
[d:aside][act:amused, a little wink]And when people are asked to fill pages with ^nonsense, they produce@verb text that looks a ^lot@amount like this.

[d:reveal][act:the reveal, lean in]Then, in {2025|twenty twenty-five}, Michael Greshko built a cipher from ^dice and playing ^cards, ordinary tools of fifteenth-century ^Italy. [p:0.93][act:explaining, step by step]Take a sentence in ^Latin, roll the dice, draw a card, and they pick how each ^letter gets written. [sfx:hit][act:delighted, slower]Out comes something very like ^Voynichese.
[d:build][act:careful, a raised finger][tune:fallrise]Not a ^solution: it doesn't decode a single ^page. [act:precise, calm]Just a way the book ^could have been made.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm][tune:rise]A real ^language inside? [act:the verdict, even][tune:fall]^*Open question*. [act:firm, matter of fact]^Every claimed decipherment so far has ^failed the test. [p:0.93][act:explaining, fair]A real reading must work on ^every page, not just the ones you ^pick.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:dreamy, weighing both][tune:fall]Beautiful ^nonsense, or a ^message nobody can read@present. [act:warm, open-ended]^Both are still on the table.
